title: Reel 2: boyhood bands with Roy Palmer, Joe Johnson and the Keppards
summary: After his brother bought him the bass, he played with Roy Palmer, Joe Johnson and Louis and Freddie Keppard, with fights over who he played with, and recalls his first Mardi Gras in 1902.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: It was around 1997 and 1999 when my brother bought that big bass for me. Uh-huh. He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, yes. Roy Palmer was our guitar player. You had to see what became a trombone player? No, let me see what Roy was playing. Roy was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And Joe Johnson was our guitar player. So Joe Johnson learned trumpet and Roy Palmer and Roy Palmer was good too. Joe died. That's what I tell the guys, they read about who they don't know. See? They read about the guys they know, see? But they had great trumpet players. I mean he was a hell of a white trumpet player, Joe Johnson. He was very good. His name was Joe Johnson? Joe Johnson, yeah. He was about the trumpet player and Freddie Kepler was a little loud trumpet player. He was a little loud trumpet player. He was a little loud trumpet player. Did you hear Baldwin? Yeah, when I was a kid. See, because Freddie, we made up a band. Eddie Goyle sent me on the job was with Freddie Kepler's brother. Louie? Louie Kepler. And I didn't know Louie was there. Louie and them had a band downtown. When I went on the job to play with Louie and them, they were trying to get a kid band. Well, that was just the thing they wanted, see? That was the biggest. Then all the bands downtown, the Imperial Band and the bands with Freddie always wanted to fight every time somebody wanted to take me out of the way up with his brother's band. Freddie wanted to fight. Freddie wanted to fight, you know? It was all right for me to play with his band, because I used to play in John Lindsay's plays sometimes, Freddie's band. Well, John Lindsay and I looked so much alike people didn't know what it is that Johnny Reed was me playing sometimes, see? Freddie wanted to fight all the time. I tell you, every time Marilyn was hiring me to play with him, and he'd get in a fight. And then King Oliver won't fight about me once. Then me and Freddie wanted to fight. Well, it wasn't no knife, it was fist, you know? So I can explain to you exactly, the closer I'd get around 19, between 7 and 9 when I first started playing string bass. But when I started, I had to be, I had to be in that, around 6. I know I was old, because I didn't start to walk and I sat on, man. I had terrified my litter. And I stopped walking, I didn't walk until I was around 5. Oh yeah. Is that so? And it had to be around 6 or 7 when I started playing. And I didn't want to play. I didn't want to do it with riding horses. That's all I used to like to do. Do you remember that first Mardi Gras that you saw? 1902, not so well. 1902. Were there a lot of brass bands? Oh yeah. They always did a lot of brass bands. I remember them when my mother came in. That's not their first one. Well that was about their first and the older one. Because after that, every year, I was, it was many years after that, every year, I was in the parade myself.
